To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the method we proposed, called "profile by category", is the most effective method among all the methods we tested in our experiments; (2) the method "profile by keyword" is the second most effective; (3) the methods "profile by term frequency" and "profile by document frequency" are the least effective; (4) the methods "term weighting" and "document ranking" do not have any effect on the performance of the systems; and (5) the methods
the method of profile generation that is based on the concept of "most frequent terms" is the best one among all the other methods tested.

(1) The proposed method is more effective than the other methods tested in terms of precision and recall, and (2) The proposed method can be used as an effective alternative to other existing methods for the profiling of consumers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two aspects.
the following questions.
a new method to generate profiles, a new unified framework and an empirical cross-system comparison of various profiling methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the most effective way to acquire users' interests is to let them specify their interests explicitly, and if that is not possible, the best way to infer users' interests is by using their past search behaviors.
the best way to profile consumers is to use a combination of methods, depending on the nature of the application.

, although all the methods tested are able to generate profiles that are effective in predicting users' information needs, they differ in terms of their ability to generate profiles that reflect users' standing interests and are effective for different users.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method is effective for profile acquisition.
, in general, the proposed method is superior to other methods, especially in the context of information retrieval.
the method of profile generation proposed in the paper is effective and can be applied in a wide range of information systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of profiling methods is highly dependent on the type of routing systems and their underlying algorithms.

, although the performance of the methods is highly dependent on the nature of the data, the methods based on the contingency theory, especially the one based on the chi-squared statistic, tend to perform better in general.

there is no one-size-fits-all solution for the profiling problem and the choice of profiling methods should be made based on the specific characteristics of the information retrieval systems and users.
